This bound and the fuller checks behind it rest on imported rigid-body mechanics under three assumptions, namely that actuator torque-speed curves remain within nominal thermal ratings, joint encoders accurately report the initial state $(\mathbf{p}_0, \mathbf{v}_0)$, and the payload mass matches the inertial model behind the actuator limits. A representative permission-path implementation monitors joint current\index{Joint current}, motor temperature\index{Joule heating}, and communication delay\index{Bus latency} at rates chosen from the plant and sensor budgets. These observations can detect some departures from the model but cannot verify every assumption, such as payload inertia, on every tick.

If motor winding temperatures exceed the thermal thresholds of @sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles, the permission path imposes thermal derating\index{Thermal derating}, scaling down the maximum allowed acceleration ($a_{\max}$) and velocity ($v_{\max}$) in the parameter registry. An external force measurement that indicates a payload mass deviation lowers the same limits. The intent filter immediately evaluates subsequent incoming leases against these reduced physical limits. A derating event can make a previously admitted path infeasible; the controller must recheck it and select a feasible fallback if the margin is lost.

When the reachability filter rejects an intent proposal, it must not simply discard the packet. Discarding without feedback leaves the upstream reasoning model unaware of why motion failed to occur, forcing it to wait for an end-to-end task timeout. The intent filter generates an immediate, structured diagnostic packet returned directly to the reasoning layer across the proposal boundary. This diagnostic payload contains the rejection classification, such as a kinematic workspace violation (`ERR_WORKSPACE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`), dynamic time insufficiency (`ERR_DYNAMIC_TIME_INSUFFICIENT`), or swept-volume collision intersection (`ERR_OCCUPANCY_BLOCKED`), along with the numerical margins of failure. For a dynamic reachability failure, the feedback returns the shortfall between the transit lower bound and the remaining window, and the maximum reachable distance along the commanded vector within the allotted lease. For a static workspace violation, the feedback provides the projection of the target onto the boundary of $\mathcal{W}$ (the closest physical point the arm can actually reach). The reasoning layer uses this structured signal to adjust its proposal on the subsequent inference cycle, by obtaining fresher evidence, choosing an alternate approach, slowing or pausing the process, or proposing base relocation. It cannot extend the evidence horizon without a new justification.

The diagnostic makes a useful staged approach possible. In the following worked branch, stipulate that the pre-contact corridor and its stopping reserve are qualified, the closer wrist observation supports the existing `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.e0_str` error bound, and the local tracker maintains the declared residual-slip bound. These are conditions of the example, not reported test results.

We first replace the rejected terminal promise with a pre-contact observation goal. The distant handle estimate does not yet support a grasp, but a separately checked corridor can support motion toward a better viewing position while preserving a stop outside contact. The closer capture supplies the mug-handle belief record whose `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.e0_str` error fits the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.r_tol_str` tolerance. The admitted target then follows that same identified mug through fresh tracker observations.

The `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.d_target_str` approach still takes at least `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_transit_floor_str`; improving sensing does not shorten the physical transit floor. The planner therefore executes guarded segments under the chunk leases of @sec-nervous-cadences, checking each continuation against the current intent, target evidence, corridor, and fallback. The overall approach may outlast the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str` horizon of any one capture because later captures support later segments. A replacement header alone cannot extend the old record, and the predicted route beyond the current admitted segment carries no execution authority.

Once the remaining approach and closure pass the full trajectory check within the then-current evidence and authority, the gripper completes the terminal grasp inside the task tolerance and transitions to the admitted hold for handover. That is the useful outcome under the stipulated conditions: the same mug reaches the handover through observed progress rather than an impossible single-window promise. If the closer observation fails, identity becomes unresolved, or a renewal arrives too late, the corresponding next segment is refused. Existing motion continues only while its own evidence, authority, and fallback remain valid; otherwise the independent controller takes the validated response. @Sec-planning constructs the timed segments and their state-matched continuations.

### Dynamic obstacle forecasting and reachable exclusion zones {#sec-intent-dynamic-forecasting}

A mug may be reachable while a coworker is about to cross the approach corridor. The workspace and transit tests alone cannot reject that conflict. **Dynamic obstacle forecasting**\index{Dynamic obstacle!reachability forecasting}\index{Dynamic reachability!exclusion cones} carries the perception and memory estimates forward into regions that moving obstacles could occupy. At the intent stage, these regions support early corridor rejection; the planner and permission path must later check the complete timed trajectory.

Consuming the dynamic track manifest $[(\text{ID}_k, \hat{\mathbf{p}}_k, \hat{\mathbf{v}}_k, \mathbf{P}_k, t_{\text{last}}, \text{state})]$ published by the multi-object tracker (@sec-perception-tracking-association), the intent filter must not treat tracked obstacles as static bounding spheres. As an obstacle moves, its future position is a time-varying spatial volume that expands forward in time. The manifest must be consumed alongside tentative detections, raw occupied regions, and unknown-space evidence: failure to confirm an identity does not make its occupied region clear. For each confirmed or coasting track $k$, the admission engine constructs the **dynamic reachability cone** $\mathcal{R}_k(\tau)$ of @eq-intent-reachability-cone over the candidate execution horizon $\tau \in [0, T_{\text{horizon}}]$:
$$\mathcal{R}_k(\tau) = \left\{ \mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3 \;\middle|\; \|\mathbf{p} - (\hat{\mathbf{p}}_k + \hat{\mathbf{v}}_k \tau)\| \le r_k + \frac{1}{2} a_{k,\max} \tau^2 + k_\sigma \sigma_{\text{track}}(\tau) \right\}$$ {#eq-intent-reachability-cone}
where:

- $r_k$ is the conservative bounding radius of the tracked entity (the illustrative $r_k = 0.35\text{ m}$ represents a torso-and-shoulder region, not a whole-person enclosure). A human exclusion model must additionally cover limbs, carried objects, and their motion under the declared operating conditions.
- $\frac{1}{2} a_{k,\max} \tau^2$ models worst-case kinematic expansion under unobserved acceleration, where $a_{k,\max}$ is the actor's physical acceleration limit (e.g., $a_{\max} \approx 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$ for agile pedestrian maneuvers).
- $k_\sigma$ is the statistical confidence multiplier (e.g., $k_\sigma = 3$, a selected multiplier whose joint spatial coverage must be calibrated, rather than inferred from a scalar Gaussian rule).
- $\mathbf{H} = [\mathbf{I}_{3\times3} \mid \mathbf{0}_{3\times3}]$ is the linear state projection matrix that maps the six-dimensional kinematic state vector $[\mathbf{p}^\top, \mathbf{v}^\top]^\top$ down to 3D Cartesian coordinates.
- $\sigma_{\text{track}}(\tau) = \sqrt{\text{tr}(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{P}_{t+\tau}\mathbf{H}^\top)}$ captures the root-mean-square spatial tracking standard deviation $\sqrt{\sigma_x^2 + \sigma_y^2 + \sigma_z^2}$, computed from the propagated covariance during sensor dropouts or coasting intervals. Its growth depends on the dynamics and position–velocity correlations; monotonic growth is not a general property. The permission check needs a conservative bound over the full interval, not an assumed increase between samples.

As illustrated in @fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones, a candidate transit corridor $\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(\tau)$ can be screened against each obstacle's reachability cone. The geometric condition in @eq-intent-dynamic-exclusion becomes a full trajectory requirement only after the planner supplies the machine's swept volume over time. Under the declared obstacle-motion and uncertainty bounds, that volume must avoid every exclusion region throughout the proposed execution window:
$$\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(\tau) \cap \mathcal{R}_k(\tau) = \emptyset \quad \forall \tau \in [0, T_{\text{lease}}], \;\; \forall k$$ {#eq-intent-dynamic-exclusion}
If a candidate corridor intersects an expanding cone, the early screen can return `ERR_DYNAMIC_OCCUPANCY_CONFLICT` and request a different corridor or a yield. The refusal diagnostic returns the earliest predicted conflict time $\tau_{\text{conflict}}$ and the conflicting actor identifier $\text{ID}_k$. Passing this screen does not establish a collision-free trajectory: the planner must supply the timed motion, and the permission path must check its swept volume and stopping reserve against evidence that remains valid.

A subtle yet critical hazard of quadratic forward reachability sets ($\frac{1}{2} a_{\max} \tau^2$) is the notorious **freezing robot problem**\index{Freezing robot problem!mitigation via short leases}. If an autonomous mobile robot projects human pedestrian reachability over a multi-second planning horizon ($\tau = 2.0\text{ s}$) with an agile sprint acceleration capability ($a_{\max} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$), the exclusion cone radius expands by $4.0\text{ meters}$. In an active industrial warehouse or crowded hospital corridor, these massive forward reachability cones overlap, instantly consuming all free space and forcing the robot to freeze indefinitely. A design can reduce unnecessary conservatism through three conditional choices. None permits shrinking a physically justified bound merely to obtain motion:

1. *Short Intent Lease Horizons:* By restricting intent leases to short, receding temporal horizons ($\tau \le 200\text{--}400\text{ ms}$), the quadratic expansion term remains tightly contained ($\frac{1}{2} a_{\max} \tau^2 \le 0.04\text{--}0.16\text{ m}$), reducing expansion over that short interval. The obstacle forecast must still cover the entire executed prefix and physical fallback, including response delay and deceleration; shortening the lease does not shorten an actor's possible motion while the robot stops.
2. *Velocity Capping:* An operating domain may justify clipping reachable sets by a validated velocity cap ($v_{\max} \approx 1.6\text{ m/s}$), transforming parabolic cones into linear cylinders for longer horizons.
3. *High-Rate Recursive Re-centering:* Qualified local trackers running at $50\text{ Hz}$ re-center the cone origin when fresh sensor measurements qualify ($t_0 \leftarrow t_{\text{fresh}}$). Those updates can reduce tracking covariance and avoid unnecessary accumulation of uncertainty, provided their accuracy and latency support the required bound.

::: {#fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Dynamic reachability cones and multi-object tracking lifecycle**: (a) Top-down bird's-eye view (BEV) of a shared workspace. A moving coworker (track 42) generates forward-expanding reachability cones $\\mathcal{R}(t)$ whose radii grow with the actor's bounded acceleration contribution $a_{\\max}$ and tracking covariance $\\sigma_{\\text{track}}$. When a proposed robot trajectory intersects $\\mathcal{R}(t_2)$, the intent gate rejects the lease with `ERR_DYNAMIC_OCCUPANCY`, requesting a detour or yield whose trajectory still requires independent admission. (b) Multi-object tracking state lifecycle, transitioning candidate detections through a chi-squared Mahalanobis validation gate and Hungarian bipartite matching into tentative, confirmed, coasting (with covariance inflation $\\mathbf{P}_{t+1} = \\mathbf{F}\\mathbf{P}\\mathbf{F}^\\top + \\mathbf{Q}$), and terminated states." fig-alt="Two-panel systems diagram. Left panel shows top-down warehouse layout with a robot planning a path toward a goal, a walking coworker with three expanding circular reachability cones R(t1), R(t2), R(t3), and a red conflict crosshatch where the path intersects R(t2) triggering an intent refusal gate. Right panel shows a state machine for multi-object tracking from sensor ingress to validation gate, Hungarian match, tentative, confirmed, coasting, and terminated states, outputting a dynamic track manifest schema."}
![](images/svg/fig10_dynamic_reachability_cones.svg){width="100%"}
:::

The two panels of @fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones connect the corridor test to the tracking evidence it consumes. The tracking lifecycle recalls the upstream evidence states: a confirmed track has fresh measurements, while a coasting track carries propagated uncertainty. Intent consumes those distinctions when bounding a goal; it does not renew a track merely by requesting motion.

The crossing corridor fails when its predicted swept volume intersects the coworker's expanding region. The resulting diagnostic asks for a detour or yield; a newly proposed route still needs its own timed check. A coasting track can widen the exclusion region as evidence ages. Terminating its software track does not make the occluded space free, so the unknown-space policy remains in force until new observations justify a different claim.

Reachability and corridor filters reject some impossible requests before planning. The survivors remain candidates, carrying the target bounds and obstacle evidence needed for the full motion check. The next distinction is between failures these physical checks can expose and errors in task meaning that they cannot settle.

## Intent Grounding Failure Modes and Affordance Invalidation {#sec-intent-failure-modes}

When a vision-language model\index{Vision-language model} or multimodal transformer outputs an $SE(3)$ target pose\index{SE(3) Kinematics} for a physical manipulator, that pose can fail in several distinct, physically hazardous ways:

1. **Phantom Target (Visual Saliency Leakage / Hallucination):** Cross-attention softmax weights spike on a specular glare, shadow, background texture, or transparent surface (such as acrylic shielding or glass beakers), causing the decoder to predict a 3D bounding volume where no solid workpiece exists. When optical depth returns are missing or corrupted by specular multipath reflection, the unprojection pipeline projects image tokens into empty space or directly inside transparent barriers. If admitted, the robot executes a futile reach into empty air or collides with invisible glass enclosures.
2. **Stale Target (Pipeline Latency / Temporal Drift):** The physical workpiece shifts on a conveyor, vibrates on a feeder tray, or is displaced by a human coworker while the multi-stage perception pipeline buffers, batches, and decodes frames. Deliberative VLA backbones running with large KV-caches on edge accelerators incur inference latencies of $200\text{--}650\text{ ms}$. The resulting proposal arrives downstream with mathematically valid coordinates that describe where the object *used to be* rather than where it *is*, consuming physical clearance before motion begins.
3. **Semantic Ambiguity (Bimodal Posterior / Argmax Failure):** Two visually identical candidate objects (e.g., two red mugs) reside within the pick zone. The network's referent distribution exhibits high entropy ($H(\mathbf{z}) > H_{\text{thresh}}$). Forcing an argmax token decode or spatial centroid averaging commands an arbitrary choice or drives the end effector toward the empty midpoint between the objects, risking a dual-object collision.
4. **Misclassified Affordance (Category Hallucination / Compliance Mismatch):** A rigid structural fixture is misclassified as a movable handle, or a thin-walled fragile container is classified as a robust workpiece, requesting grip forces that shatter the item. The trajectory planner generates a geometrically collision-free approach, but the physical wrench envelope commanded by low-level impedance loops destroys the mechanism upon contact.
5. **Dynamic Unreachability (Kinematic Transit Shortfall):** A requested terminal move is geometrically within the static workspace manifold $\mathcal{W}$, but the transit time demanded by actuator velocity and acceleration limits exceeds the remaining sensor evidence window ($t_{\text{transit}} > \tau_{\text{lease}}$). The terminal request must be rejected or replaced with guarded stages supported by fresh observations; extending its old evidence deadline cannot make it feasible.

Despite their varied mathematical origins across attention heads, depth triangulation, and latency tails, all five failures arrive downstream across the proposal boundary in the exact same format: a candidate coordinate vector $\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and orientation $\mathbf{R} \in SO(3)$.

The downstream planner receives a dated target proposal, not an actuator command. A pose on an empty location may lead to a futile reach; a pose inside an occupied fixture may lead to contact if the later path and permission checks fail. In the wrong-object case, by contrast, the geometry can be valid while the selected object is semantically wrong. The independent permission path therefore checks what it can measure (freshness, coverage, geometry, current state, and actuator limits) without claiming to verify the task's meaning. **The Safety MCU enforces physical feasibility, not semantic truth: a goal can be perfectly collision-free, kinematically smooth, and torque-limited, yet completely wrong for the task.** If a vision-language model confuses an expensive optical lens with a compliant rubber puck, the downstream controller will execute a smooth, authorized grasp that fractures the lens. Semantic verification belongs to upstream task monitoring and operator oversight; the physical permission path can enforce its declared physical bounds only while their sensing, model, timing, and actuator premises hold.

A fresh depth observation can reject a proposed grasp whose required object evidence is absent in a covered, visible region. No return in an occluded or unobserved region leaves it unknown. For this station, the selected singulation rule requires independently qualified evidence of a single candidate in the pick window, even when the grounding model is confident. A window with multiple candidates leaves this operating mode and goes to a coworker for manual selection. This is a scoped operating choice: another qualified mode could select a uniquely identified mug among several objects. Counting itself needs validated coverage and segmentation; it cannot establish that the lone object is a mug. The producer's entropy filter may refuse earlier but cannot replace the station's independent check.

@Tbl-10-grounding-failure-modes groups these failures by the check that can expose them. Dynamic transit insufficiency can be rejected before motion, whereas a misclassified affordance may first become observable through contact residuals. The table separates admission checks from responses after motion or contact has begun. At the cage-door latch of \ref{nbk-intent-lease-duration-collision-exposure-tradeoff-across}, the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_contact_str` contact-loop response already leaves `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_at_brake_onset_n_str` at brake-command onset, and the peak comes later, so precontact speed and force limits, actuator response, compliance, and available clearance determine whether the full contact trace stays within the validated contact limits.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}

| Failure mode                                                             | Evidence or check                                                                                                              | Admission or response                                                                                          | Physical limit to verify                                                                                                            |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Phantom target:** image artifact in empty space                        | Fresh depth evidence and target-region occupancy, with coverage and occlusion checked                                          | Reject the proposal when the required object evidence is absent; request another view if the region is unknown | Rejection precedes motion only if the proposal has not already been admitted. Missing returns alone do not prove empty space.       |
| **Stale target:** workpiece moved after capture                          | Converted capture time, bounded clock error, local tracking, and target-error envelope                                         | Revoke dependent tracking when the evidence limit fails; select the validated fallback                         | Total detection, communication, actuation, and braking delay must fit the measured clearance.                                       |
| **Station singulation failure:** multiple candidates in the pick window  | Independent count of candidates in the pick window from fresh depth evidence; model entropy as an earlier producer-side signal | Refuse admission and route the item to the coworker for a manual pick                                          | A single wrong object passes the count, and a confident model can report low entropy; independent physical checks remain necessary. |
| **Misclassified affordance:** bolted fixture selected as graspable       | Contact-force and motion residuals after contact; precontact task/geometry checks where possible                               | Limit precontact speed and force, then invoke the validated contact response on a threshold crossing           | A reactive trip does not cap the first impact peak; test the full force trace, response delay, and stopping energy.                 |
| **Dynamic unreachability:** target cannot be reached in its valid window | Speed-ceiling transit lower bound followed by a complete path and stopping check                                               | Reject terminal completion on that record; consider separately admitted guarded segments                       | Passing the lower bound proves neither collision-free motion nor a feasible stop.                                                   |

: **Grounding failure modes and their evidence limits**: Each check addresses a different failure class. The table separates proposal rejection from a response to an already moving plant. {#tbl-10-grounding-failure-modes tbl-colwidths="[19,27,25,29]"}

Every row of the table therefore requires the proposal to carry its spatial bounds, the provenance of its evidence, and its expiry, in a form the permission path can check without the model. A rejected proposal returns a reason to the learned layer. It does not itself revoke an earlier active record, which remains usable only while its own state, evidence, lease, and fallback hold. An admitted proposal remains subject to independent permission checks as the plant moves. The proposal carries those fields across the proposal boundary, and the record the permission path grants from it is the intent lease.

## The Intent Lease Specification and Contract {#sec-intent-lease}

For the red mug, the engineering result is a target region that the evidence can still support, a limit on the effort used to pursue it, and a deadline after which tracking must stop. The intent lease preserves that decision for downstream consumers. Its parent is the belief record of @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema, named by digest, and its evidence time comes from that record's evidence epoch converted to the MCU's monotonic clock. The admitted target constrains planning; it supplies neither a continuous path nor permission to execute one.

In the machine stack's 14-record contract lineage, this stage emits the **Intent Specification** (Contract 9). While the uncertified Application Processor proposes an untrusted candidate intent proposal (@tbl-10-intent-proposal-fields) across the proposal boundary (@sec-intent-four-stage-pipeline), the Safety MCU independently evaluates and latches the admitted **Intent Specification** record (realized at runtime as the active **Intent Lease**). This cyber-physical contract binds high-level semantic intent to verified geometric goal sets, affordance frame transforms, and admitted task predicates, constraining the downstream trajectory planner (@sec-planning-behavior-seam) before any motion is admitted.

The candidate proposal uses a statically bounded record so the permission path can reject malformed fields and bound ingestion work.[^fn-intent-intercore-channel] Fixed-size fields avoid unbounded allocation and pointer traversal, but constant record size alone does not prove a deadline: copying, cache maintenance, synchronization, and contention still need a measured bound. The wire layout and platform-specific transport obligations are collected in @sec-appendix-systems-wire-intent and @sec-appendix-systems-ipc. The message carries a request; configured limits, the deadline, and the state-dependent fallback remain under the independent controller's authority.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ **Byte layout:** The intent payload's fields, types, and offsets are given in @sec-appendix-systems-wire-intent.
:::

[^fn-intent-intercore-channel]: **Inter-core communication across the proposal boundary**\index{Inter-core communication!RPMSG}\index{Proposal boundary!inter-core communication}: RPMSG over a statically bounded shared SRAM ring is one transport. Copy count, cache maintenance, coherency, and worst-case handoff time depend on the system-on-chip (SoC) and driver, and the MCU's independent timer detects lost renewals even through a host kernel panic. See @sec-appendix-systems-ipc.

The covariance ellipsoid of the mug-handle estimate in @sec-intent-request-to-proposal is a producer-side localization estimate. The proposal does not attempt to serialize a general oriented $3\times3$ covariance matrix across the wire; its bounds carry three conservative **position-error envelopes** $(e_x,e_y,e_z)$ and three requested **task tolerances** $(r_x,r_y,r_z)$ in the named robot-base frame instead. Envelope and tolerance maintain the strict distinction established in @sec-intent-grounded-affordances: admission mandates $0\le e_i\le r_i$ on every axis. The producer must justify any conversion from raw covariance to a conservative error envelope, including camera calibration uncertainty and declared tail risk. Orientation tolerances and contact-mode rules originate from an independently approved task profile; the proposal carries only the nominal target orientation itself.

The proposal's evidence time is the **belief record's evidence epoch**, never its estimate epoch, converted to the MCU's clock domain under the clock synchronization rules of @sec-nervous-cadences. The MCU matches both the parent digest and that epoch to the bounded retained belief evidence supplied through the qualified local interface, adding the clock mapping's bounded conversion error to its age evaluation. The requested expiry uses the same monotonic clock, enabling the MCU to compare it directly with physical evidence and braking stopping deadlines. The parent digest establishes **data lineage and auditability, not message authentication**, under the integrity policy of @sec-nervous-cadences: it links the proposal to its perceptual origin, allowing post-incident telemetry analysis to trace a commanded action back to raw camera photons. The intent proposal carries no cryptographic signature because the permission path admits it by empirical physical content and invariant checks, not by sender identity.

The admitted intent transitions through five formal states: `Pending`, `Active`, `Renewed`, `Expired`, and `Aborted`. The MCU transitions to `Active` only after validating the request against independently configured ceilings and verifying that a collision-free fallback trajectory remains feasible from the current physical state. A renewal requires a strictly increasing sequence counter, a fresh parent belief record with an advanced sensor capture timestamp, and a re-evaluated permission check; it does not automatically extend execution authority. Satisfying the terminal task predicates while the supporting lease remains valid completes the goal; an approach can span several properly renewed leases. A contact-limit violation or loss of required evidence revokes dependent tracking. A missed sensor frame need not revoke it before the validated coasting bound expires, but it cannot renew that bound. Revocation initiates a physical response rather than instantaneously stopping moving mass.

::: {#dfn-intent-expiring-intent-lease .callout-definition title="Expiring intent lease"}

***Expiring intent lease***\index{Expiring intent lease!definition}\index{Intent lease!definition} ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) is a time-bounded target authorization issued by the independent permission path that binds an admitted target pose and effort ceilings to a monotonic hardware deadline $t_{\text{exp}}$:
$$t_{\text{exp}} = \min(t_{\text{evidence}} + \tau_{\text{ev}}, \; t_{\text{adm}} + \tau_{\text{lease}}, \; t_{\text{stop\_deadline}})$$ {#eq-intent-lease-expiry-bound}
upon whose expiration dependent target-tracking authority is automatically revoked without requiring an explicit cancellation packet. The lease constrains a separately admitted trajectory; it does not authorize a path by itself.

1.  **Significance**: Withdraws tracking authority on a hardware deadline when upstream deliberation stalls, so the validated fallback starts without waiting for the proposer.
2.  **Distinction**: Unlike a network keepalive or software ping, an intent lease couples the horizon of physical sensor evidence ($\tau_{\text{ev}}$) with dynamic braking feasibility, and its expiry falls no later than the stop deadline at which a validated fallback still fits the remaining clearance.
3.  **Common pitfall**: Sizing lease durations generously to mask tail latency ($P_{99}$) in neural inference, which creates an unmonitored open-loop window where the robot moves through an environment that may have changed.

:::

The three terms in the minimization enforce fundamentally distinct safety bounds that prevent different classes of failure across the cyber-physical stack:

- $t_{\text{evidence}} + \tau_{\text{ev}}$ is the **physical target validity horizon**: the absolute monotonic-clock instant when unobserved physical drift, vibration, or workpiece slip causes the true object position to diverge beyond the task tolerance $r_{\text{tol}}$. Rooted in the sensor transduction epoch $t_{\text{evidence}}$ rather than packet transmission time, this bound reflects the physical decay of sensory information. Under linear drift rate $v_{\text{drift}}$ and initial state estimation error $e_0$, the validity horizon elapses at $\tau_{\text{ev}} \le (r_{\text{tol}} - e_0) / v_{\text{drift}}$. Once this horizon expires without fresh perceptual confirmation, the robot moves toward an ungrounded hallucination, regardless of whether the upstream software stack is executing normally.
- $t_{\text{adm}} + \tau_{\text{lease}}$ is the **software administrative lease**: an explicit upper bound on how long the deliberative Application Processor (AP) is permitted to retain motion authority before the Safety MCU presumes host failure, measured from the monotonic hardware admission tick $t_{\text{adm}}$. Even if the physical workpiece is completely stationary ($\tau_{\text{ev}} \to \infty$), an uncertified host running Linux, ROS 2, or PyTorch cannot be granted unbounded open-loop authority. Operating system scheduling jitter, garbage collection pauses, neural inference timeouts ($P_{99}$ latency spikes), or host kernel panics can freeze the deliberative planner. The administrative lease $\tau_{\text{lease}}$ bounds the host's maximum unmonitored execution window, ensuring that a deadlocked planner triggers safe deceleration rather than runaway open-loop extrapolation.
- $t_{\text{stop\_deadline}}$ is the **physical stopping boundary** for the current state and selected response: the latest authority-revocation deadline from which the budgeted response can stop the robot. It reserves command transport and actuator onset before braking, so that physical stopping distance ($d_{\text{stop}} = v \tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2a_{\text{brake}}}$) does not violate available obstacle clearance. If clearance along the robot's swept volume is $d_{\text{clear}}$, continuing tracking past $t_{\text{stop\_deadline}} = t_{\text{adm}} + (d_{\text{clear}} - d_{\text{stop}})/v$ exhausts the reserve for this declared response. For this deadline calculation, $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ contains only the bounded interval from scheduled authority revocation through its interrupt or tick handling, command transport, and physical braking onset. The waiting interval before revocation is already represented by the deadline and must not be charged again. Clearance is evaluated at admission after accounting for observation age. The expression assumes $v>0$, constant speed while waiting, and the stated braking model; at $v=0$, use a stationary hold and obstacle-approach assessment instead of dividing by speed. Changing speed, clearance, or actuator capability requires recomputation.

By evaluating the minimum across all three terms on the Safety MCU's monotonic hardware clock, the architecture requires motion authority to terminate at whichever validated margin is exhausted first: physical evidence decay, host software silence, or kinematic clearance limits. At expiration, an independent hardware timer interrupt revokes tracking authority and the MCU initiates whichever of its validated fallback responses—powered hold, controlled path deceleration, or torque disable—is appropriate for the measured dynamic load and contact state. The proposal's requested terminal mode is purely advisory; an upstream model requesting torque disable over a suspended payload cannot override the powered hold mandated by the safety controller. Neither a `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_permission_str` check period nor a hardware interrupt establishes a physical stop within a single period: stopping is a mechanical process governed by inertia, requiring pre-reserved stopping clearance before any motion is admitted.

The proposal's fields support layered checks, cheapest first, and one implementation orders them in this bounded admission sequence:

1. **Evidence and sequence:** Read a complete proposal packet. Reject an old sequence or a parent digest and evidence epoch that do not match a retained belief record. Compute evidence age in the MCU monotonic domain and add the bounded clock-conversion error. Reject when that age exceeds the target-evidence horizon.
2. **Proposal limits:** Check finite pose values, quaternion normalization, base-frame error and task-tolerance axes, and requested wrench against approved task and actuator limits. Check known occupancy and unknown-space policy.
3. **Dynamic admission:** Use current velocity, clearance, and actuator state to reject proposals that already fail a lower bound on transit time. Require that the total sensing-to-brake-onset travel plus braking distance fit inside the current clearance before granting motion. If no feasible fallback exists from this state, refuse the proposal. Under this station's singulation rule, refuse also when qualified fresh evidence shows more than one candidate in the pick window, and route the item to the coworker for manual selection. This stage admits a target and effort ceilings, never a path; admission of the whole trajectory belongs to the planner's record (@sec-planning-behavior-seam).
4. **Authority latch:** Store only the MCU-approved target, effort ceilings, expiry no later than the evidence deadline, and selected fallback. Arm the local timer for the admitted interval. The untrusted requested expiry and terminal mode do not control the drive directly.
5. **Runtime check:** On each configured control tick and relevant hardware fault event, compare measured state with the admitted limits. On evidence expiry, missed renewal, or an observed violation, revoke the proposal and start the previously validated response. The ensuing braking and hold have their own measured delay and physical margin.

When the Safety MCU latches an admitted proposal in Stage 4, it emits the admitted target record consumed by the trajectory planner (@tbl-10-intent-specification-contract).

| `goal_region`            | `double[3]` (m), `double` (rad) | Spatial semi-axes $(r_x, r_y, r_z)$ and angular tolerance $\theta_{\text{tol}}$                                               | Defines $SE(3)$ goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ (@eq-intent-goal-set-se3); terminal boundary     |

: **Intent Specification contract record (Contract 9)**: Schema, data types, physical semantics, and invariant checks for the admitted target contract emitted by the Safety MCU and consumed by trajectory planning. {#tbl-10-intent-specification-contract tbl-colwidths="[20,18,32,30]"}

The **Intent Specification** contract record (@tbl-10-intent-specification-contract) acts as the formal contract boundary between spatial memory and trajectory planning. By anchoring `parent_belief_digest` to the upstream `SpatialBeliefRecord` (Contract 8, @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema) and emitting its own `intent_digest` to the downstream `TrajectoryRecord` (Contract 10, @sec-planning-behavior-seam), it creates an unbroken, auditable custody chain from raw camera photons to motor currents. Trajectory planners cannot alter the admitted geometric goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ (@eq-intent-goal-set-se3), nor can they extend tracking beyond `expiration_deadline_ns`.

Filled in for the red mug, the lease admitted for the pick carries six entries. Its parent is the mug-handle belief record of @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema, matched by digest and evidence epoch. Its goal is the handle pose, and its error envelope is that record's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.e0_str` initial error, inside a `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.r_tol_str` task tolerance. Its evidence horizon is the age at which the governing growth law reaches that tolerance, `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str` under the record's belt-drift law and `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str` under the residual-slip law of the qualified tracker's renewed record. Its speed ceiling is the arm's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.v_tcp_str` tool-center-point speed limit, and it requests no item-specific wrench ceiling, because none is registered for the mug. The configured task and actuator ceilings still bound the wrench, and fragility is handled by the site's control of which items reach the conveyor, not by the controller. Its task objective is grasp, then hold for the handover, although the MCU still selects the fallback from its approved responses. Its expiry is the earliest of that evidence horizon, the configured lease ceiling, and the stop deadline.

This record gives @sec-verification a concrete interface for fault-injection tests in which corrupted quaternions, stale capture records, oversize force requests, and incompatible terminal requests should each be rejected under the tested state and timing conditions.

::: {#chk-intent-wire-schema-watchdogs .callout-checkpoint title="Expiring intent and fallback authority"}

Verify your understanding of how a proposal is refused or admitted, and how the lease granted from it is sized and revoked:

- [ ] **Ambiguity refusal**: Why does this station's singulation rule refuse a pick window holding two candidates, and why must that test run on a confident proposal as well as an uncertain one?
- [ ] **Wrong-object premise**: Which premise about the grasped object remains outside the permission path even when every coordinate, reachability, and force check passes, and where does the machine carry that premise instead?
- [ ] **Evidence horizon**: Can you explain why the evidence horizon of an intent lease is bounded by task tolerance and target drift rather than by the reasoning model's period, and why inflating it to hide tail inference latency leaves motion on an obsolete target?
- [ ] **Clock domain**: Why must the MCU convert the belief record's evidence epoch into its own monotonic clock, with a bounded conversion error, before checking age and the requested expiry?
- [ ] **Fallback selection**: Can you explain why the MCU must select a feasible approved hold, deceleration, or torque-disable response from the measured load state rather than obey the proposal's requested terminal mode?

:::

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-intent-fallacies-pitfalls}

Each mistake in this section trusts an upstream message to mean more than it does. Local checks\index{Local checks!authority withdrawal} must refuse a target, or withdraw tracking authority over one, when its evidence expires or its physical justification dissolves, and they must decide on evidence the proposer does not control, even while its messages remain well formed and confident.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *A renewal computed from the same stale frame is a valid renewal.*

In distributed computing and cloud infrastructure, lease renewals operate as software heartbeats: a client process demonstrates liveliness and retains its lease simply by transmitting an uncorrupted keepalive packet before the timeout elapses. In physical AI, however, software liveliness has zero correlation with physical evidence validity.

Consider an intent model that re-reads its last captured wrist-camera frame of the red mug and transmits a renewal with an incremented sequence number, a later issue time, and the identical target pose. Every field a standard network keepalive or RPC liveness check inspects has advanced normally. Yet no new photons have struck the camera sensor since the original capture that justified the target, and the physical mug has continued drifting along the takeaway conveyor at `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.v_conveyor_str`. Because the intent lease anchors its evidence clock strictly to the parent belief record's sensor transduction epoch $t_{\text{evidence}}$\index{Lease!evidence epoch}, not to proposal transmission or packet arrival time, the Safety MCU detects that the physical evidence epoch has not advanced. The MCU continues counting evidence age from the original physical capture, enforcing expiration `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str` after that original frame. A controller that dated renewals by message arrival would allow a tight, unmonitored software loop to maintain tracking authority over an obsolete coordinate indefinitely, transforming transient target drift into a permanent collision hazard. **Advancing software timestamps on stale sensory data creates an illusion of liveliness while unobserved physical drift violates clearance.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Anchor lease validity strictly to the sensor evidence epoch $t_0$ of the parent belief record; reject renewals that fail to supply a qualified newer capture record, including its error bound and bounded clock conversion.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Allowing an unexpired temporal lease to continue commanding motion when target spatial bounds are violated.*

In distributed locking protocols, a lease grants exclusive, unconditional authority over a resource for the entire duration of its temporal grant. In physical AI, however, an intent lease is a coupled spatio-temporal contract:
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \left( \mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}, \; [t_{\text{adm}}, t_{\text{exp}}], \; \mathbf{w}_{\max} \right)$$
Temporal freshness ($t < t_{\text{exp}}$) is a necessary condition for motion execution, but never a sufficient one.

Suppose the robot arm lowers its end effector toward the red mug under an admitted intent lease with the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.r_tol_str` grasp tolerance. An unexpected conveyor belt slip or workpiece collision shifts the physical mug beyond that tolerance while substantial time still remains on the hardware lease timer. Although the temporal lease remains active, the physical target has exited the $SE(3)$\index{SE(3)!spatial bounds} goal region $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ that justified the approach trajectory. Continuing execution until the countdown timer elapses would drive the arm toward an empty coordinate or collide with a displaced obstacle. The selected permission loop must compare the latest qualified target evidence and its age-dependent bound against the admitted spatial limits, revoking tracking authority when a checked update shows that the spatial containment condition $\|\mathbf{p}_{\text{target}}(t) - \hat{\mathbf{p}}_{\text{target}}\|_2 \le r_{\text{tol}}$ is breached. The loop cannot detect an unobserved slip merely by checking faster; sensing delay and error growth must remain in the response budget. Encoding the invariant lets the controller withdraw tracking authority without waiting for host replanning or timer expiry once the violation is detected. **A temporal lease confers authority only within declared spatial bounds; temporal freshness never excuses spatial divergence.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Embed runtime spatial containment checks ($E(\Delta t) \le r_{\text{tol}}$) in high-rate control loops, revoking dependent authority when qualified evidence or its propagated bound no longer supports the tolerance mid-lease.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *A confident grounding needs no refusal path.*

In machine learning and natural language processing, a high softmax or sigmoid probability ($p > 0.99$) is often treated as definitive proof of class identity. Engineers transitioning to physical robotics frequently attempt to optimize pipeline latency by implementing shortcut logic: `if confidence > threshold: skip_ambiguity_checks()`. This design treats the model's subjective confidence score as an objective audit of the physical environment, creating three critical points of failure:

1. **Neural miscalibration and open-vocabulary bias:** Deep vision-language models trained with cross-entropy loss are notoriously overconfident on out-of-distribution inputs. An open-vocabulary detector will readily assign a $0.98$ confidence score to a glass jar or printed decal if it represents the closest semantic match in the prompt token vocabulary.
2. **Relative classification versus physical uniqueness:** Softmax normalization enforces a probability distribution over candidate tokens or classes; it does not measure real-world uniqueness. If two identical red mugs sit side-by-side in the pick window, an uncalibrated detector may assign high confidence to one mug due to subtle crop or lighting variations, performing an arbitrary $\operatorname{argmax}$ that masks genuine scene ambiguity.
3. **Severe physical consequence:** A confidence score is a diagnostic of the model's internal parameter agreement, not a guarantee that the physical workspace contains exactly one manipulable entity. In @sec-intent-request-to-proposal, a glass jar beside the red mug arrives with a high confidence score and a tight bounding box, precisely where an ambiguity refusal was mandatory.

The station's singulation check\index{Refusal!confident grounding} must execute on every proposal, drawing on evidence that the vision-language model does not produce. An independent candidate-counting check operating directly on calibrated spatial point clouds or voxel occupancy grids evaluates the physical workspace: if the pick window contains more than one candidate cluster, the system refuses the proposal with `ERR_GROUNDING_AMBIGUITY` and returns the selection failure regardless of model confidence. Any earlier active record remains subject to its own evidence, lease, and fallback; a hold or human handoff requires the corresponding feasible transition. **Neural softmax confidence reflects internal model agreement, not real-world uniqueness; an ungrounded argmax can select the wrong physical object.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Enforce the selected station's singulation rule using qualified independent candidate evidence; treat `ERR_GROUNDING_AMBIGUITY` as a first-class diagnostic that can request a feasible hold or operator handoff without automatically revoking a still-valid active record.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Neural networks can resolve bimodal spatial ambiguity by averaging candidate target locations.*

In end-to-end imitation learning and behavioral cloning, Mean Squared Error (MSE) favors a single prediction that averages unresolved alternatives. A deterministic policy $\pi_\theta(\mathbf{x})$ trained on demonstration dataset $\mathcal{D} = \{(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{y}_i)\}$ minimizes the empirical $L_2$ regression loss:
$$\min_\theta \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) \sim \mathcal{D}} \left[ \|\mathbf{y} - \pi_\theta(\mathbf{x})\|_2^2 \right]$$
For the corresponding population loss, finite conditional second moments and an unrestricted predictor yield the conditional mean as the optimum:
$$\pi^*(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\min_{\hat{\mathbf{y}}} \int \|\mathbf{y} - \hat{\mathbf{y}}\|_2^2 \, p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x}) \, d\mathbf{y} = \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x}]$$

A finite network trained on finite data need not attain this population optimum: model capacity, sampling, and optimization affect the result. The mean nevertheless exposes the ambiguity that the squared-error objective rewards.

Now consider a physical pick-and-place scenario where two identical red mugs, $A$ and $B$, sit side-by-side on the takeaway conveyor at coordinates $\mathbf{y}_A$ and $\mathbf{y}_B$. In the training demonstrations, human operators pick Mug $A$ half the time and Mug $B$ half the time. The true target distribution conditioned on visual observation $\mathbf{x}$ is bimodal:
$$p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2}\delta(\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{y}_A) + \frac{1}{2}\delta(\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{y}_B)$$
Here $\delta$ denotes a point mass at each candidate location, so the model assigns equal probability to the two exact targets. When evaluated on this multimodal distribution, the MSE minimizer collapses to the spatial centroid:
$$\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x}] = \frac{\mathbf{y}_A + \mathbf{y}_B}{2}$$

In abstract representation learning, regression to the mean produces a blurry image or an interpolated feature embedding. In physical manipulation, however, the configuration space $\mathcal{C}$ and collision-free workspace $\mathcal{W}_{\text{free}}$ are non-convex sets. The midpoint $\frac{\mathbf{y}_A + \mathbf{y}_B}{2}$ lies in empty space between the two mugs, or worse, directly on an intervening barrier. Commanding the end effector to this centroid drives the gripper into empty air, missing both targets, or collides with the inner edges of both mugs, risking severe joint overload.

The machine sees two identical red mugs set a few centimeters apart on the takeaway conveyor and receives their spatial mean as a grasp target. Suppose both detections pass their association and innovation gates (@sec-memory-belief-through-occlusion) and each retained hypothesis is sharp. Their physical existence alone would not guarantee those results: the gates compare measurements with predicted tracks. The window check of @sec-intent-failure-modes still catches the case, because it counts two candidates in the pick window and the admission gate\index{Admission gate!rejection} refuses the new proposal, whatever the fused estimate reports. That refusal does not revoke a still-valid active record; if a transition to hold is needed, it must remain physically feasible. A covariance gate\index{Uncertainty!covariance expansion} would catch it only for an estimator that reports the bimodal ambiguity\index{Bimodal ambiguity!spatial}, which an averaging estimator does not.

This fundamental failure of unimodal regression under multimodal data is why modern physical AI architectures utilize expressive generative modeling (such as Diffusion Policies, Flow Matching, or Mixture Density Networks) to preserve full multi-hypothesis distributions. However, at the **Grounded Intent proposal boundary**, systems safety cannot depend on the policy's internal generative mechanics. The intent proposal passed across the proposal boundary must commit to a single discrete, certified geometric goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ anchored to a unique entity tracking digest, never an interpolated spatial average. Furthermore, this station's independent candidate-counting gate enforces its singulated pick window, rejecting multi-candidate scenes with `ERR_GROUNDING_AMBIGUITY` before any motion trajectory is synthesized. **Averaging bimodal physical targets can replace two valid manipulation candidates with a location that satisfies neither task.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Preserve explicit multi-hypothesis distributions at the reasoning boundary (via diffusion policies or Gaussian mixture models), and enforce discrete candidate selection backed by the independent pick-window ambiguity gate.

:::

## Summary {#sec-intent-summary}

Grounded intent resolves the fundamental systems mismatch between unconstrained semantic reasoning and deterministic physical execution. A large foundation model or vision-language-action policy proposes a candidate target in $SE(3)$, bounded error envelopes, and requested effort ceilings. The Safety MCU acts as an independent gatekeeper for untrusted proposals: it admits a bounded target through the active **Intent Lease** (Contract 9), anchored to a parent belief record in spatial memory (@sec-memory). The lease bounds operational validity to a strict monotonic hardware deadline derived from physical target drift ($\tau_{\text{ev}}$), host administrative silence ($\tau_{\text{lease}}$), and kinematic stopping clearance ($t_{\text{stop\_deadline}}$). The independent countdown initiates revocation through bounded interrupt or control-tick handling when the deadline elapses. That response delay belongs in the stopping budget; the fallback does not wait for the stalled deliberative host.

The red mug on the conveyor makes the multi-rate cadence constraint concrete. Its untracked evidence lasts `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str`, and the machine's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_intent_str` intent model, refreshing every `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_intent_period_str`, cannot maintain that target by itself. A qualified local tracker can refresh it from new evidence and lengthen the horizon to `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str`, leaving the intent model only to re-confirm which mug is meant; otherwise the machine slows, pauses, or refuses the task. With the stipulated corridor, closer observation, and qualified tracking, the longer approach succeeds through separately admitted segments and a terminal grasp that fits the current evidence. Expiry invokes a response validated for the measured state; it cannot undo momentum already injected into physical links.

What grounded intent adds to physical AI is formal capability sandboxing: bounding semantic uncertainty into geometric affordance manifolds before trajectory optimization, and treating refusal (`ERR_GROUNDING_AMBIGUITY`, `ERR_DYNAMIC_TIME_INSUFFICIENT`) as a first-class control outcome. A terminal request that cannot finish on its current evidence fails the transit lower bound; guarded progress may instead use fresh observations and renewed segments. A pick window holding two candidates fails this station's singulation rule, and each rejection returns structured diagnostics the proposer can act on. The wrong-object case marks the immutable epistemic boundary of physical verification: a confident grounding to the wrong physical entity passes every coordinate, reachability, and force check. That premise requires its own perceptual evidence and operator oversight, because geometric and effort checks cannot establish object identity, and their own physical guarantees remain conditional on validated premises.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Grounded intent at the proposal boundary"}
* **A lease grants a target, never a path:** The Brain supplies a target, evidence epoch, error envelope, task tolerances, and requested expiry, and it writes no actuator setpoints. The permission path admits a target and effort ceilings that expire at the earliest of the evidence horizon, the lease ceiling, and the stop deadline.
* **The Intent Specification emits verified goal sets:** The 9th contract in the contract lineage binds admitted affordance frames, validated motion predicates, and geometric goal regions into an immutable record consumed by trajectory planners.
* **Evidence expires with drift:** Target drift and task tolerance set a finite validity horizon under a declared validity region. A fresh timestamp does not make a target correct, and only fresh evidence, never a faster model, renews it.
* **The evidence deadline is not the motion deadline:** The permission path separately budgets sensing, communication, enforcement, actuator delay, and braking distance for the current state and clearance.
* **Geometry cannot verify meaning:** A confident grounding to the wrong object can pass every coordinate, reachability, and force check. That premise needs its own task evidence, because the permission path cannot settle it.
* **Refusal is an admissible outcome:** Ambiguous identity, stale evidence, insufficient reachability, or infeasible stopping can each reject a proposal, and a structured rejection tells the proposer what to change. Each check has its own evidence limit.
:::

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From intent leases to trajectory planning"}
The intent lease fixes the target region, effort ceilings, and evidence deadline. It leaves the path unresolved. @Sec-planning constructs a timed motion and a matched stopping continuation within those bounds, recording them in the Trajectory Record (Contract 10). The independent permission path must admit that complete proposal before execution; a valid goal alone cannot establish that the moving machine can stop.
:::
